title: Introduce toolchain-autopilot, compact presubmit runner, and dep-reshuffle
author: Eleanor Park
description: Motivation: Our presubmit and release flows have accumulated ad-hoc toolchain manifests per repo and a heavy unified lint runner that adds latency to iteration. This PR introduces a small, opt-in 'toolchain-autopilot' daemon for CI that selects and materializes minimal toolchain manifests at presubmit time, a compact 'presubmit-lite' runner for quick feedback on common changes, and a dep-reshuffle helper to move rarely-used transitive deps into an opt-in dev-only bundle. Goals: reduce CI wall time for common PRs, shrink presubmit resource usage, and make repository toolchain upgrades safer and incremental. Design notes: - toolchain-autopilot uses .redwood/ci.toml in a repo to locate language profiles (python/node/go) and desired tool versions; when missing it falls back to a repo-heuristic. - presubmit-lite is a lightweight workflow that runs on path-sensitive triggers and executes a constrained subset of linters and fast unit tests; fuller suites are still run on the main CI lanes and nightly smoke. - dep-reshuffle is a scripted suggestion engine (scripts/dep-reshuffle.py) that proposes moving dev-only transitive deps to dev bundles and produces a patch to package manifests; the team still reviews before applying. Rollout plan: opt-in flag in repo config for initial 30% of repos, monitor presubmit latency and merge rate for 2 weeks, expand if stable. Checklists: - [x] Implement autopilot materializer and unit tests - [x] Add presubmit-lite workflows (GitHub Actions) - [x] Add dep-reshuffle script and local CLI - [x] Add telemetry for presubmit duration and toolchain cache hit-rate - [x] Add documentation in docs/ci/toolchain-autopilot.md - [ ] Monitor and iterate (post-merge) Change summary: - ci/toolchain/autopilot.go: new materializer service with cache and fallback heuristics - .github/workflows/presubmit-lite.yml: new fast-path workflow that runs on path filters - scripts/dep-reshuffle.py: analyzer and patch generator for package manifests - docs/ci/toolchain-autopilot.md: explainer and opt-in instructions - internal/telemetry/presubmit_metrics.go: new metrics for presubmit latency and cache hit-rate - ci/actions/toolchain-bootstrap/: small sharable actions to prepare micro-images - build/Makefile: expose a new 'ci-autopilot-test' target Tests and CI: unit tests added for autopilot heuristics, presubmit-lite includes smoke steps in Actions; end-to-end integration was validated on a canary repo (redwood-examples/ci-canary). Backwards compatibility: no repo is migrated automatically; the default behavior remains the existing toolchain until .redwood/ci.toml opt-in is present. Migration doc links included. Why this is different from previous CI refactors: rather than a monolithic rewire of all presubmit jobs, this PR provides an opt-in, minimal surface for teams to get quick wins and observable outcomes.

commit_summary: Introduce materializer that emits minimal toolchain manifests for a PR
Provide dep-reshuffle script to propose dev-only transitive dependency moves
Add telemetry for presubmit latency and toolchain cache hit-rate
review_comments: Luca Moretti: Nice incremental approach — please add a fallback test that simulates missing .redwood/ci.toml and validates heuristic outcomes.
Aisha Khan: Can we gate presubmit-lite behind a feature flag to avoid bursty runs during rollout? Also request that the action logs include a correlation id for debugging.
Priya Desai: dep-reshuffle looks useful but can be dangerous for mono-repo manifests; add a dry-run mode and stricter heuristics for top-level packages.
author_responses: Eleanor Park: Added fallback unit test (autopilot_test.go) and documented the heuristic behavior in the doc. The fallback is also covered in the canary run.
Eleanor Park: Presubmit-lite is behind a repo opt-in flag in .redwood/ci.toml; the action will no-op unless opt-in is set. Added correlation IDs to the action logs.

Eleanor Park: dep-reshuffle now defaults to dry-run; we only generate a suggested patch and a rationale that requires manual approval before apply. Updated heuristics to skip top-level workspace manifests by default.
ci_checks: presubmit-lite smoke: executed in canary and returned expected exit codes
release_notes: Introduces toolchain-autopilot (opt-in), a lightweight presubmit workflow (presubmit-lite), and a dep-reshuffle helper. Opt-in via .redwood/ci.toml. Reduces presubmit latency for opt-in repos; non-breaking.
notes_for_oncall: If presubmit latency spikes after rollout, toggle opt-in flag per repo and check autopilot cache hit-rate metric (telemetry.autopilot.cache_hit_rate). For dep-reshuffle false positives, consult suggested_patch.log in the PR artifacts.
post_merge_todo: 1) Monitor presubmit latency and cache hit-rate for 14 days; 2) Run dep-reshuffle across selected dormant repos in dry-run; 3) Iterate heuristics based on false positive rate.
